basis: Derived from the handout ordering rule and the raw changes_batch02.csv / curated.csv rows, before reading Role C Silver exports.

predictions.B_C01_stale: All 10 keys R003001-R003010 arrive with an OLDER ingest time than the current Silver row; Silver v1 keeps the baseline observations_a.csv rows unchanged. Example R003005: keep row 3005 (18.50 C, ingest 01:03:30Z), reject batch row 125 (17.50 C, 01:03:00Z).
predictions.B_C02_tied: 10 keys carry two batch revisions with identical ingest time and source_object; the smaller source_row wins. R002005: row 105 (20.50 C) beats row 140 (21.50 C) and, being newer than baseline row 2005 (18.50 C), updates Silver. R010005: new key, row 5 wins over 135.
predictions.B_C03_order: Winners are identical for every input order (both orders of every tied pair, reversed and 200 random shuffles).
predictions.B_C04_predicate: The actual merge_silver SQL predicate updates only on newer ingest, or equal ingest with smaller source_object, or equal ingest+object with smaller source_row; equal identity and stale rows (even with smaller object/row) are no-ops.
predictions.B_C05_replay: Second application: stale keys stay unchanged_stale, tied winners become unchanged_equal; Silver v2 rows for these 20 keys are identical to v1.
predictions.B_C06_gold: Each stale batch value is 1.00 C below the kept value and each superseded tied value is 1.00 C above its winner. Stale-overwrite would therefore lower 2026-02-03 sums by 5.00 for zone-1 (S01-S05) and zone-2 (S06-S10): 16046.00->16041.00, 16406.00->16401.00. Last-row-wins would raise zone-1 2026-02-02 by 5.00 (13972.50->13977.50) and zone-1 2026-02-06 by 5.00 (532.50->537.50). Actual Gold v1 shows neither.
